statusDetail: 55 of 58 checks were conclusively judged. End-to-end sign-in, passkey availability, and authenticated account-management safety were blocked because no Yahoo test credentials were available.

page.notes: Public Yahoo authentication utility. Representative public archetypes: sign-in, account recovery, and account creation. Authenticated/password/passkey/account-management states were not covered.

checkOutcomes.method: Dark-mode screenshot plus computed-style DOM probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Under emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark, the page remains a white/light-only surface; computed html color-scheme is light.
The reduced-motion probe confirmed the preference matched and found zero active animations on the login surface.

checkOutcomes.method: Screenshot under prefers-contrast: more and forced-colors: active
checkOutcomes.evidence: Forced-colors/high-contrast capture retains visible text, borders, controls, checkbox state, and links.
The login, recovery, and account-creation journey changes views without any authored View Transition CSS; probe found no view-transition rules.
No parallax, scrollytelling, carousel, or scroll-linked motion exists on the compact authentication surfaces.
checkOutcomes.reason: No parallax, scrollytelling, carousel, or scroll-linked motion exists on the compact authentication surfaces.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No gesture-driven control, swipe action, carousel, or scroll-snap interaction exists on the audited authentication surfaces.
checkOutcomes.reason: No gesture-driven control, swipe action, carousel, or scroll-snap interaction exists on the audited authentication surfaces.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The compact sign-in and recovery forms have no meaningful scroll-reactive chrome; account creation is a conventional linear form.
checkOutcomes.reason: The compact sign-in and recovery forms have no meaningful scroll-reactive chrome; account creation is a conventional linear form.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No tooltip, popover, anchored menu, or transient overlay is present on the audited surfaces.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip, popover, anchored menu, or transient overlay is present on the audited surfaces.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Strong heading hierarchy, auto-focused first field, prominent Next button, and inline focus return after validation make the next step and moved attention clear.
No popup, consent wall, or interstitial obscured the authentication forms on load across three routes.
No overlay, disclosure, picker, or other dismissible transient control is present to require dialog/popover/details semantics.
checkOutcomes.reason: No overlay, disclosure, picker, or other dismissible transient control is present to require dialog/popover/details semantics.

checkOutcomes.evidence: At desktop width, a large animated-looking Yahoo Finance promotion consumes about half the first viewport and competes with the primary sign-in task.
At 360x800 the form reflows to one column; layout reports 360px scrollWidth, 360px clientWidth, and 0px horizontal overflow with viewport meta present.
The same authentication card changes from a desktop side panel to a full-width mobile card while preserving field and action hierarchy; no reuse context showed a failed component state.
Primary controls are 52px tall, keyboard focus is visible, and Lighthouse target-size passed; the 18px checkbox has a larger associated text label.
“Sign in to Yahoo”, the username label, and a single prominent Next action make the page purpose and next step immediately clear.

checkOutcomes.method: Attempted sign-in with empty and synthetic non-existent identifiers, plus recovery-route inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: The unauthenticated username and recovery steps were exercised, but end-to-end sign-in requires a valid Yahoo account and secret; no credentials were available.
checkOutcomes.reason: The unauthenticated username and recovery steps were exercised, but end-to-end sign-in requires a valid Yahoo account and secret; no credentials were available.

checkOutcomes.evidence: A synthetic non-existent username produces only “Whoops, something went wrong.” It gives no cause, retry advice, or account-recovery link in the error itself.
Lighthouse measured 5.1s LCP (performance 69) and the raw trace measured 7.1s LCP; both are outside the good threshold.
Mobile layout observation measured CLS 0.00287 and Lighthouse measured 0.00014, both comfortably in the good range.
Trace total blocking time was 85.59ms with two long tasks; Lighthouse TBT was 233.5ms, elevated but not the dominant load failure.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR dependency summary confirmed against live script attributes
checkOutcomes.evidence: The main document took 4.94s; four parser-inserted, non-async/non-defer analytics/consent scripts are in head, and one analytics script lacks compression and cache headers.
The simple sign-in form transfers 705KB across 24 scripts; Google Tag Manager alone is 169KB and third-party requests account for 841KB of 862KB total.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse axe audits and DOM semantics probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 100; the form probe found explicit labels for username and persistence controls, accessible action text, and alt text for both logos.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse contrast audit and high-contrast screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast passed with no failing nodes, and forced-colors preserved essential content.
A main landmark and headings are present; all interactive controls accepted visible keyboard focus, and invalid submission returned focus to #username.
Text remains clear and unclipped at desktop and 360px, with readable labels and instructions on sign-in, recovery, and account-creation views.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile layout, viewport and Lighthouse audits
checkOutcomes.evidence: The mobile layout reflows without horizontal overflow, user scaling is not disabled, Lighthouse target-size passed, and there is no time-based media requiring captions.
Lighthouse found no errors logged to the browser console.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM, image audit, and Lighthouse best-practices evidence
checkOutcomes.evidence: The document has valid HTML/UTF-8, but both Yahoo logo images omit width and height; one lacks srcset and both are legacy PNG.
Lighthouse reports the page is ineligible for back/forward cache for two reasons, reducing clean browser-history restoration.
The page exposes a descriptive title and meta description in the rendered DOM; Lighthouse title and description audits passed.
All visible links have real href values and descriptive text, viewport meta is present, robots.txt permits the root login page, and Lighthouse crawlable-links passed.

checkOutcomes.method: Auth-surface applicability judgement plus robots/sitemap probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: This is a deliberately gated authentication utility, not a public content page intended for indexing; a sitemap is not required for the login endpoint.
checkOutcomes.reason: This is a deliberately gated authentication utility, not a public content page intended for indexing; a sitemap is not required for the login endpoint.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The page is an authentication utility, not an article, product, event, place, or other rich entity that needs JSON-LD or social-preview metadata.
checkOutcomes.reason: The page is an authentication utility, not an article, product, event, place, or other rich entity that needs JSON-LD or social-preview metadata.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The page uses HTTPS, HSTS, CSP, nosniff, X-Frame-Options DENY, strict-origin referrer policy, and all observed cookies are Secure; no sensitive client-side secrets were found.
The login load contacts 9 third-party origins, including Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics; 46 of 48 requests and 840,830 transferred bytes are classified third-party.

checkOutcomes.method: Load observation and attempted unauthenticated auth-flow inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: No permission prompt fired on load and Google federation is visible, but passkey/WebAuthn availability can only be established after identifying a real account; no account credentials were available.
checkOutcomes.reason: No permission prompt fired on load and Google federation is visible, but passkey/WebAuthn availability can only be established after identifying a real account; no account credentials were available.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Permissions-Policy is absent and CSP allows all style origins plus unsafe-inline, weakening browser-enforced least privilege despite strong HSTS and frame denial.

checkOutcomes.method: Discoverability raw-HTML comparison and crawler screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: Raw HTML contains 82% of rendered content and is not a JS shell; with JavaScript disabled the page shows a clear sign-in limitation and a Try again recovery action rather than a blank shell.

checkOutcomes.method: Route screenshots and validation focus probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The audited forms contain no overlays or fragile menus, retain focus through validation, and render consistently across desktop/mobile route changes.
Authentication intrinsically requires an online identity service; no offline completion is meaningful, so a service worker/manifest is not expected for this standalone login endpoint.
checkOutcomes.reason: Authentication intrinsically requires an online identity service; no offline completion is meaningful, so a service worker/manifest is not expected for this standalone login endpoint.

checkOutcomes.method: Crawler adverse-state screenshot and validation probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The no-JavaScript/adverse state is an explicit “We couldn’t sign you in” page with troubleshooting and Try again; validation errors remain in context with focus returned to the field.
The served locale declares html lang=en-GB and dir=ltr; audited copy is coherent for that locale and mobile layout survives narrow reflow.
The unauthenticated sign-in and recovery views display no dates, numbers, currency, durations, or locale-sensitive data.
checkOutcomes.reason: The unauthenticated sign-in and recovery views display no dates, numbers, currency, durations, or locale-sensitive data.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The audited authentication surfaces contain no times, events, recurrence, or time-zone-sensitive concepts.
checkOutcomes.reason: The audited authentication surfaces contain no times, events, recurrence, or time-zone-sensitive concepts.

checkOutcomes.method: Initial desktop/mobile screenshots and form-state probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: “Stay signed in” is selected by default, opting users into persistent authentication even on a shared device unless they notice and reverse the choice.
Errors appear only after submission, set aria-invalid=true, use role=alert, return focus to the username field, and the empty case clearly says “This is required.”
The username/email/phone field has an empty autocomplete attribute instead of autocomplete="username", preventing reliable password-manager and sign-in autofill assistance.

The public sign-in, recovery, and create-account entry views were inspected, but cancellation, sensitive-action reauthentication, passkey management, and authenticated account controls require a real account.
checkOutcomes.reason: The public sign-in, recovery, and create-account entry views were inspected, but cancellation, sensitive-action reauthentication, passkey management, and authenticated account controls require a real account.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Both logos are PNG without intrinsic dimensions; one lacks responsive sources. The assets are small, but modern format/dimension metadata is not fully used.
A simple login form initiates 48 requests and 705KB of scripts, including analytics, consent, and tag-manager work before authentication.
Third parties account for 46 of 48 requests and 840,830 of 861,889 transferred bytes, disproportionate to the value of the unauthenticated login form.
Authentication is a security-sensitive flow with no declared agent-facing surface; exposing sign-in credentials as WebMCP tools is not an expected requirement.
checkOutcomes.reason: Authentication is a security-sensitive flow with no declared agent-facing surface; exposing sign-in credentials as WebMCP tools is not an expected requirement.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The login/recovery flow has no summarisation, generation, or language-inference task for which on-device AI would improve the experience.
checkOutcomes.reason: The login/recovery flow has no summarisation, generation, or language-inference task for which on-device AI would improve the experience.

checkOutcomes.method: Baseline/repeated heap summaries plus same-session performance.memory/DOM sampling
checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten alternating invalid/empty submissions, a retained heap summary was 17.1MB versus 15.75MB baseline while DOM nodes remained exactly 138 in the same-page probe. The modest one-time growth is consistent with loading validation code and does not show unbounded accumulation.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap summary totals and constructor distribution
checkOutcomes.evidence: Baseline retained self-size was 15.75MB for the hydrated sign-in application; this is not unusually large for the observed Next.js/auth/analytics surface.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap constructor summary and same-session DOM sampling
checkOutcomes.evidence: No Detached-named constructor appeared among retained top constructors, and ten repeated submissions left live DOM count stable at 138; no accumulating visual animations were present.

principleOutcomes.reason: Authentication is a security-sensitive flow with no declared agent-facing surface; exposing sign-in credentials as WebMCP tools is not an expected requirement. The login/recovery flow has no summarisation, generation, or language-inference task for which on-device AI would improve the experience.

paths.description: Primary public sign-in form, including preference, mobile, keyboard, empty-submit and synthetic unknown-account states.
Forgotten-username/account-recovery entry archetype; represents public recovery before identity verification.
Account-creation entry archetype; reviewed for mobile layout and public form structure.

findings.summary: Light-only styling ignores the user’s dark preference
findings.evidence: The dark-mode capture remains white and computed html color-scheme is light.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light and dark schemes early, set color-scheme: light dark, and theme surfaces/text with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.evidence: No authored View Transition rules are present across sign-in, recovery, and creation route changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document or cross-document View Transitions for directional continuity, while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Desktop promotion competes with the sign-in task
findings.evidence: The Yahoo Finance promotion occupies roughly half the desktop first viewport beside the authentication card.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce or defer promotional creative on the security-sensitive login surface so authentication remains the uncontested focus.

findings.evidence: A synthetic unknown username returns only “Whoops, something went wrong.” with no reason or recovery action in the message.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a privacy-safe, actionable message with retry and account-recovery options, announced through the existing alert region.

findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 5.1s and the DevTools trace measured 7.1s.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the performance guidance to shorten document latency, prioritize the LCP content, and defer non-critical work.

findings.summary: Parser-blocking analytics and consent work delays delivery
findings.evidence: Four classic scripts in head have neither async nor defer; the main document took 4.94s and opus.js is uncached/uncompressed.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical analytics/consent scripts, compress and cache static code, and keep the critical dependency chain focused on the form.

findings.summary: The login form ships a heavy JavaScript payload
findings.evidence: The page transfers 705KB in 24 scripts; GTM alone is 169KB and most bytes are third-party.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused and duplicate code, conditionally load analytics, and split authentication-critical code from optional integrations.

findings.summary: Logo assets omit intrinsic dimensions and responsive metadata
findings.evidence: Both logos omit width/height, one lacks srcset, and both are PNG.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic width/height, responsive sources where useful, and consider AVIF/WebP or an appropriate vector while preserving alt text.

findings.summary: The page cannot use the back/forward cache
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports two BFCache failure reasons.
findings.suggestedFix: Inspect the Lighthouse BFCache reasons and remove avoidable unload handlers, cache-control blockers, or incompatible APIs.

findings.summary: Tracking footprint is excessive on the login page
findings.evidence: Nine third-party origins are contacted; 46 of 48 requests and 840,830 bytes are third-party, including GTM and Google Analytics.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise authentication-page telemetry, remove unnecessary third parties, and batch or defer analytics until justified by user action/consent.

findings.evidence: Permissions-Policy is absent and CSP style-src allows all origins plus unsafe-inline.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a least-privilege Permissions-Policy and tighten style-src with nonces/hashes or bounded origins after report-only testing.

findings.summary: Persistent sign-in is enabled by default
findings.evidence: The Stay signed in checkbox is checked on first load, including on a potentially shared device.
findings.suggestedFix: Default persistence off or make device trust explicit and contextual, preserving a clear reversible choice.

findings.summary: The username field does not advertise autofill semantics
findings.evidence: The field accepts username/email/phone but its autocomplete value is empty.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete="username" and retain the clear label so password managers and browser autofill can assist reliably.

findings.summary: Image delivery misses lightweight asset techniques
findings.evidence: Two logos use PNG and omit intrinsic dimensions; one has no srcset.
findings.suggestedFix: Add dimensions and responsive/modern image delivery appropriate to these small logos.

findings.summary: Background analytics work is disproportionate to the form
findings.evidence: The unauthenticated form initiates 48 requests and 705KB of scripts before the user acts.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritize and conditionally load background analytics so sign-in-critical work wins.

findings.evidence: Third parties contribute 840,830 of 861,889 transferred bytes and 46 of 48 requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party budget for authentication, remove low-value vendors, and defer remaining integrations.
